newsitem.title: USA: Northwest committee aims to retain power benefits.
newsitem.headline: Northwest committee aims to retain power benefits.

text.p: A committee appointed by the governors of Idaho, Montana, Oregon and Washington late last week completed draft recommendations for restructuring the Northwest electricity system.

The proposals aim to ensure that Northwest electricity customers benefit from the emerging competitive market for electricity while preserving reliability, benefits of the region's low-cost hydroelectricity, and environmental values.
The changes are designed to protect the region's commercial, industrial and residential ratepayers as well as natural resources, said committee chairman Chuck Collins.
The recommendations will be available for public comment from next week through mid-November. The committee will submit a final report to the governors in December.

* To keep the benefits of low-cost federal hydropower in the Northwest, the proposal called for Northwest utilities and other power suppliers to contract for most of the hydropower output at cost on a long-term basis. Others could purchase on shorter-term contracts.
Mechanisms were also proposed to ensure that fish recovery needs are met while limiting costs borne by subscribers.

* To ensure that electricity customers would be able to choose among various providers, regulators and local utility boards and commissions should be prepared to offer open access to electricity for all customers by 2001.

* To promote environmental quality, utilities and state regulatory commissions should dedicate three percent of the revenues from the sale of electricity services in the region every year for the next 10 years to sustain investments in energy conservation, renewable resources and low-income weatherization.

* To encourage competition in electricity supply and maintain reliable electrical service, an independent transmission grid operator should be created with broad membership, including Bonneville and the region's other major transmission owners.
